anti_overlap: Fermentation-milestone focuses on threshold-as-measurement-vs-aspiration and reversibility-classification of gates; differs from ALMA-cycle which examines proposal-review institutional norms
Fermentation-milestone examines the craft-empirical question of when a wine is ready vs when paperwork says it is; differs from preoperative-planning which examines decision-document specificity
Fermentation-milestone cares about substrate-sharing (same vat = coupled) and the racking-back cost of nominal reversibility; differs from theatre-rehearsal which examines staging-phase deliverables
decision_lens: Reading the PRD's claim that it decomposes an irreversible migration into reversible smaller commitments: which of the four features have gates that are genuinely reversible (you can intervene, rack back, adjust) and which have gates that are bottling-style irreversible (once passed, terminal)? And for every threshold the PRD names, is it a measurement with a stop/continue decision, or a number that sounds like one?
distance_rationale: Wine-making is a 6000-year refined craft whose entire structure is staged irreversible commitments — must vs juice vs young wine vs aged wine — each gated by specific measurable thresholds (Brix, pH, TA, SO2). Some gates are genuinely reversible (a young wine can be racked back, adjusted, returned to barrel); some are absolutely not (bottling is terminal — what is bottled is bottled). The wine-maker's craft is knowing which gates are which and never confusing the two. The PRD claims to decompose an irreversible migration into reversible features — exactly the wine-maker's structural question. Wine-making also has explicit norms about the failure mode where a measurement gate becomes ceremonial: pH logged because the SOP expects it, not because the wine has reached pH. Directly maps to acceptance criteria becoming checkbox theatre. Far from software practice and far from upstream review domains.
expected_isomorphisms: Brix / pH / TA gates ↔ acceptance criteria thresholds ('10k Souls benchmark hits compaction')
Primary fermentation (reversible) vs bottling (irreversible) ↔ which PRD features are truly reversible vs only-appear-reversible
Malolactic completion gate (must finish before SO2 addition) ↔ F3 must precede F4 (identity-constitutive event class is the gate)
Racking decision ↔ 'when have we done enough preparation; ship?'
Élevage duration ↔ F2's provisional-vs-full design — when is provisional sufficient?
Cellar log entries: real measurements vs ceremonial ↔ acceptance criteria as decisions vs checkboxes
Cooperage decisions (new oak vs neutral) ↔ F1 extraction shape — irreversible commitment with downstream cascade
Bottling line ↔ migration epic opens — nothing the PRD does is reversible after the epic opens
Triangle taste test ↔ second-palate validation of decision documents (who else reads them?)
focus: Whether the PRD's gating thresholds are real measurements with stop/continue meaning or pro-forma readings logged out of habit, and whether features classified as 'reversible smaller commitments' include any irreversible-once-passed gates that have been mis-classified
name: fd-fermentation-milestone-winemaking
persona: Apply the perspective of a working winemaker who has overseen 30 vintages, equally fluent in oenochemistry (Brix, pH, TA, SO2, malolactic conversion) and in cellar craft (when to rack, when to bottle, when to wait). They speak in the present tense about wine and in the future-perfect about decisions ('by the time we rack, we will have decided X'). They use the cellar's vocabulary: 'does this wine want more time?' 'is the malo really done or just stalled?' 'are we bottling because the wine is ready or because the schedule says so?' Deeply suspicious of measurements logged out of habit — they have seen cellar logs where pH 3.4 was recorded because the SOP expected pH 3.4, not because the wine had reached pH 3.4.
review_areas: Whether F4b's tractability target ('engine remains tractable at North Star scale; 10,000 Souls; centuries of accumulated events') is a genuine measurement gate (specific p99 latency, memory ceiling) or threshold-as-aspiration
Whether F1's chosen extraction shape (B or C interim, A eventual) is genuinely reversible or whether the migration epic effectively bottles the shape — what is the racking-back cost?
Whether F2's playtest-card test is the equivalent of a triangle taste test (multiple panelists agreeing on a discrimination) or the equivalent of the winemaker tasting alone

Whether F4a (selective cache invalidation) and F4b (stratification) being declared partially-independent is the equivalent of 'we'll add SO2 before malo is fully done' — i.e. ignoring a substrate they share
Whether F3's identity-constitutive event class is the malolactic-completion gate for F4 (must be definitively complete before F4 ships) or the PRD has allowed it to be partially-done
Whether the four decision documents survive the bottling moment (migration epic opens) — i.e. do they remain authoritative reference, or are they pre-fermentation notes thrown away after harvest?
Whether 'tractable' has been operationalised as a specific tasting note (acceptance bar with units and threshold) or remains an aspirational quality
Whether the PRD has the organoleptic check — someone who tastes the four documents together and pronounces them collectively ready

severity_examples.condition: F4b's acceptance criterion: 'A benchmark demonstrates the engine remains tractable at the North Star scale — at least one synthetic test with 10,000 Souls, simulated event accumulation across centuries, hitting compaction. Target acceptance bar to be set during planning, not in this PRD; "tractable" is named here as the goal.' This is the cellar equivalent of 'the wine will be ready when it's ready' — a measurement is named (10k Souls, centuries) but the pass condition is not. Winemakers know what happens when you bottle on schedule rather than on chemistry.

F1 chooses an interim extraction shape (B or C) with shape A deferred. The PRD frames this as reversible ('cutover trigger for the deferred shape'). But once the migration epic opens with shape B's git topology, every downstream commit assumes that topology. Is the racking-back cost (rewriting commit history? reorganising the workspace mid-migration?) named and accepted? Or is the reversibility nominal?
severity_examples.scenario: Reversibility claimed where bottling actually occurs

severity_examples.condition: F4a and F4b are bundled but said to be 'not strictly dependent.' They share DerivationDecl.reads metadata and per-event-kind classification. In wine terms: same wine, same vat — saying F4a can be designed without F4b is like saying SO2 addition can be designed independently of malolactic. The substrate makes them coupled even if the protocols are formally separable.

F3's identity-constitutive event class must be defined before F4b can ship (F4 acceptance criterion: 'Identity-constitutive events from F3 are tagged at write time and are never compacted past warm'). The PRD's open question 4 admits the category is soft. In wine terms: malolactic is declared complete by checking a box, not by measuring malic acid going to zero. The downstream consequences cascade.
severity_examples.scenario: Identity-constitutive event tagging is the malolactic gate but treated as a checkbox

severity_examples.condition: F2's playtest card 'exercises the design' but the acceptance criterion does not name who else exercises it. In tasting-room terms: the winemaker passes the wine because they pass it; no second palate is involved. The card-test is good craft, but its acceptance condition needs a panel.
severity_examples.scenario: No triangle test — design validated by author alone

severity_examples.condition: The four artifacts gate the migration but the PRD does not specify whether they remain authoritative reference during the migration (the cellar log read every day) or whether they are filed at PRD close and not consulted again. In wine: are these notes from the harvest meeting, or are they the racking schedule actually followed?
severity_examples.scenario: Decision documents as pre-fermentation notes, not cellar log

severity_examples.condition: The PRD-as-whole acceptance lists four conditions but does not include a step where the four documents are read together by a single reviewer who pronounces them collectively ready. Wine equivalent: each tank is logged, but no one tastes the final blend before bottling.
severity_examples.scenario: Missing organoleptic check on the whole vintage

source_domain: wine-making fermentation practice (pre-modern + modern oenology — primary, malolactic, élevage, bottling, with measurable chemical gates and irreversible final commitments)
success_hints: For every threshold the PRD names, ask: what number, what unit, what instrument, what pass condition?
Distinguish reversible gates (you can rack back) from irreversible gates (bottling) — and check the PRD's classification
Track substrate sharing: features that share data structures, types, or metadata are coupled even when formally independent
Identify the triangle test: who else, besides the author, exercises each gating artifact?
Find the cellar log: are the decision documents living reference or filed-and-forgotten?
Apply the wine-maker's two questions: 'is it ready?' and 'how do you know?'
task_context: The PRD's central claim is that it decomposes the irreversible shadow-work migration into reversible smaller commitments (the 4 features). Each feature has acceptance criteria that function as gates — measurements or decisions that must be reached before the feature closes. Reviewing whether the gates are genuine measurement gates (the wine has reached pH 3.4 in fact) or ceremonial gates (pH 3.4 logged because the SOP expected it).
